title: Apache Spark Connect is falling back to classic local mode by default
question:
I'm trying to use Apache Spark Connect from PySpark (version 4.0.0) with the following config:

spark1 = SparkSession.builder \
    .config("spark.api.mode", "connect") \
    .config("spark.connect.server.address", "sc://192.x.x.x:7077") \
    .config("spark.connect.disable.fallback", "true") \
    .config("spark.sql.catalog.spark_catalog", "org.apache.spark.sql.delta.catalog.DeltaCatalog") \
    .getOrCreate()

df = spark1.createDataFrame([{"name": "Alice", "age": 30}, {"name": "Bob", "age": 25}])
df.show(truncate=False)

Even when the Spark Connect server is not running, the session is created successfully at http://localhost:4040, and I’m able to create DataFrames and execute actions like df.show() without any errors.

This should not happen, because I have explicitly set

.config("spark.connect.disable.fallback", "true")

My expectation is as below: -

The session should fail immediately if Spark Connect cannot reach the server.

Instead, the below activities: -

  1. Spark silently falls back to classic mode, even though fallback is explicitly disabled.

    Spark UI is visible at localhost:4040, confirming that a local JVM SparkContext is being used.

I even tried the below code: -

spark = SparkSession.builder \
    .config("spark.api.mode", "connect") \
    .config("spark.connect.grpc.binding", "172.29.249.139:7077") \

But I am getting the same result. This does not fully satisfy the actual purpose of spark connect. Also, the fallback is happening by default although it is disabled.

If this is a bug in spark 4.0.0 package, then when is the fix getting released. If this is an expected behavior, then please let me know.

But I am not satisfied with the expected behavior because it doesn't fulfil the actual purpose of spark connect.

Let me know please.
answer:
I solved my own problem. Now I am able to connect to WSL from windows and run the python spark application from windows using WSL resources.

Below steps had solved my problem: -

  1. Go to $SPARK_HOME/conf in WSL

  2. Edit the spark-env.sh file and add the below lines

    export SPARK_MASTER_HOST=<WSL_IP>

    export SPARK_LOCAL_IP=<WSL_IP>

  3. Start your master and worker in WSL

  4. submit your spark job from windows using

    spark-submit --master spark://<WSL_IP>:7077 --deploy-mode client testing_remote_spark.py

But if you check your run logs you will find unable to set spark.api.mode to connect.

So, it still suspect spark connect is not fully ready in spark 4.0.0
